events.summary: Discover the story of American craftsmanship in Handmade: The Crafting of America. Explore why we make, how we innovate and the people we create for.

events.title: Awakening the Dragon–Showcasing the Building and Performance of an Asian Icon
events.summary: Experience a curated experience of the imaginary, featuring a lightly sci-fi, magnificent work of art--the LRCCS Fortune and Longevity Dragon, a 25-ft long, Asian-inspired full-body dragon sculpture for use in the traditional "dragon dance" crafted by renowned international artist Zhen Guo with U-M faculty arts lecturer Raymond Wetzel, artist Jeri Rosenberg, students, and volunteers The exhibition highlights the story of the dragon's fabrication and its impact on community.. An iconic symbol of inclusivity, strength, and courage, this newly imagined U-M dragon, with its futuristic flair, technological creativity and sustainable materials, invites students and the entire community to re-envision a classic cultural symbol for contemporary times. Presented by the Lieberthal-Rogel Center for Chinese Studies. This project was made possible by grants from the University of Michigan Arts Initiative and the Office of the Provost, Global Engagement. Additional funding was provided by ArtsEngine, Center for World Performance Studies, Stearns Collection of Musical Instruments, and U.S. Department of Education. events.title: The Tree of Eternity
events.summary: The Tree of Eternity is an immersive, interactive installation that explores remembrance, loss, and the enduring presence of those we have loved. The installation centers on a projected tree surrounded by interactive terminal pods that control its structure. Visitors approach interactive pods positioned throughout the gallery space, where they are invited to recall memories of people or experiences throughout their lives. Depending on the kiosk they interact with, different effects will be present on the projected tree. As more visitors’ memories are inputted, the tree’s visuals adapt and change form, demonstrating that our memories persist with us. Projection mapping creates ethereal visuals accompanied by atmospheric audio. Even when visitors aren't actively engaging with the kiosks, the system generates ambient transmissions, suggesting that the tree—and the memories it embodies—continues to live and grow. The installation creates a dialogue between life and death, presence and absence, individual memory and collective remembrance, inviting participants to contribute to a living memorial that persists beyond any single moment of grief or reflection.

events.title: A Holiday to Never Forget | All of Human History, Lightly Abridged
events.summary: With the Holidays in full swing, surrounded by light and family, one can only reflect on how another year is ending, and all the years before it. Join us for a night where we look back, ALL the way back, to the beginning of humanity itself. Over the course of an hour the impeccable historians of Never Forget will reenact all of human history, perfectly and unabridged. Luckily we’ll have the help of our audience members to join us on stage as supporting characters (but fear not gentle reader, no one participates who doesn’t want to!). Those who don’t learn history are doomed to repeat it. Or at least reenact it. Join us for a night you’ll Never Forget.

events.title: cART-ography: An Arts, Culture, and Sustainability Workshop
events.summary: Countermapping is a radical way to use the tools of mapping in a way that engages with our environment in a politically explicit way. It can bring to light hidden histories of structural environmental discrimination, subvert dominant claims about space, and highlight ongoing struggles for decolonization and justice. In this workshop, we’ll think about the political dimensions of mapping, geography, and the environment, especially in the local context. Then, we’ll create our own countermaps using collage, a fun medium friendly to all levels of artistic experience. Plus, dinner is provided!

events.title: Stephen Rush presents a Fluxus Concert
events.summary: Professor of Performing Arts Technology Stephen Rush presents an afternoon full of Fluxus events and compositions. Is it theater? Is it music? Is it Art? Come see. The audience will see, hear, and experience *audience-friendly* Fluxus compositions by John Cage, La Monte Young, Yoko Ono, Michael Gould, Ben Patterson, Toshi Ichiyanagi, Matthew Evan Taylor and some compositions – never-before-performed – written by Rush when he was nine years old. As they enter the lobby of the school, the audience will be greeted by 4 Fluxus compositions that are participatory in nature. Fun for the entire family. FACULTY BIO https://smtd.umich.edu/profiles/stephen-j-rush/

Equal parts comedy, heartfelt drama, and action-packed adventure, the play celebrates the power of great storytelling and the geek and warrior in all of us. She Kills Monsters is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Samuel French, Inc. For more information, visit www.concordtheatricals.com.

events.title: Wild Beauty by jessica Care moore
events.summary: Experience an unforgettable evening of poetry, music, and healing with Wild Beauty, an original experimental opera created by acclaimed Detroit poet jessica Care moore. Blending spoken word, opera, jazz, soul, and orchestral composition, this multidisciplinary work features an ensemble of artists including composer De’Sean Jones, pianist Jon Dixon, opera soul soprano Kisma Jordan, vocalist and composer Shara Nova, and Detroit soul artist Ideeyah.

evidence.description: This experimental talk has two parts. In the first 30 mins, I'll explain our proof of the join-meet positivity using geometric Satake. featuredEvents.summary: The University of Michigan's Concert Band presents "For All," a program celebrating liberation and diversity. This performance features works by contemporary composers, reflecting on the USA's 250th anniversary with music that honors various communities and ideals.

In conjunction with the USA's 250th anniversary, this concert features works that celebrate the liberation of all people: women, LGBTQIA, Latino, African American, and those Americans that dared to think differently and seek a "more perfect union."
